title: Each door machine calls in every 30 seconds, and nothing watches what that adds up to
what: A door machine is told to check in every 30 seconds, all day and night. That is about 2,900 calls a day per machine to MettleUp's door service, and each call makes up to three calls to the gym server. Cloudflare's free plan allows 100,000 calls a day for the whole account, so about 30 machines would use it up on their own, before any desk or member traffic. Nothing counts the door service calls and nobody at MettleUp is warned as they climb. Once the allowance runs out, machines get an error, keep their punches, and no member visits show at any gym until the next day. Not live today: the door service is written but not switched on.
expected: Machines check in no more often than needed, door service calls are counted with the rest, and MettleUp is warned well before the daily allowance runs out.
who: owners and members of gyms with door machines
how_often: every day once enough machines are added
fix_line: Make machines check in less often, count door service calls, and warn MettleUp before the daily limit

title: Anyone can call the door service with made-up machine numbers as often as they like
what: The door service answers any caller, and each call with an unknown machine number writes to the gym server. Nothing limits how often one sender may call. Someone sending made-up numbers in a loop would use up the free daily call allowance for every gym, and also push out the list of 'machines we can see calling' (it keeps only 5,000), so a real owner adding a new machine would no longer be told it was seen. Not live today.
expected: Calls from unknown machines are limited per sender, and the 'seen calling' list cannot be flooded out.
who: all gyms; owners adding a machine
fix_line: Limit calls per sender and per unknown machine number before writing anything

title: A machine with a big backlog of punches may be refused again and again
what: The gym server refuses any single upload with more than 5,000 punches, and the door service cuts any upload larger than 2 MB. A machine that was offline for weeks, or a busy gym's machine, may send more than that at once. The refusal comes back as an error, the machine keeps the same punches and tries the same upload again 30 seconds later, so it can stay stuck and send nothing new. If the upload is cut at 2 MB instead, the punches past the cut may be lost without a word. How big a machine's uploads get depends on the machine model and is not known.
expected: A large catch-up upload is saved in parts, or the machine is told to send smaller batches, and the owner is told when a machine is stuck.
who: gyms whose machine was offline a long time
fix_line: Save large uploads in parts and warn the owner when a machine keeps failing

title: An open payment link asks the server every 4 seconds for as long as the screen stays open
what: While a payment link is on the desk screen, the app asks the server every 4 seconds whether it has been paid. It keeps asking when the tab is in the background or the desk has walked away, until the link is paid, cancelled or runs out, and links last for days. One screen left open overnight makes about 20,000 calls a day, all counted against the same free daily allowance every gym shares.
expected: The app slows down after the first few minutes, stops asking while the tab is hidden, and relies on the payment company telling the server when money comes in.
who: gyms using online payments; every gym through the shared allowance
how_often: whenever a payment screen is left open
fix_line: Slow the checks down over time and pause them while the screen is hidden
